script: I basically financially ruined my family through shortselling. I have lost pretty much everything because of my (in hindsight admittedly very stupid) investment idea. I never went to business school or even college, but I hustled, learned on the job, and taught myself skills like a boss. I got a wife, opened a little shop that sold Kinder Surprise Egg Toys, and survived the grind. It was rough, I cut a lot, but eventually I was chillin' in the local collectors market—stable, enough to say "I got this." Then I got all hyped about short selling Korean fried chicken companies. The logic: Korean population dropping, people going vegan, healthier food trending, so chicken is going to flop. I did my "research" on consumer trends, thought I'd strike gold, and I shorted every chicken company in Korea. I was like, "I am going to make bank, no cap." But then—plot twist—Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang strolled into a Korean chicken joint called Khanbu Chicken in Seoul. He posted a pic with fried chicken and beer, and the whole internet lit up. Stocks of Korean chicken firms jumped 20-30% overnight. I got margin called, my positions blew up, and my account went to zero. Literally insane. Now I haven't even told my family. If they ask why we can't travel or afford a better apartment, I say I am reinvesting all of this. "We will reap the rewards soon," I brag, because, honestly, I am the best. (I know, right?) Since then, I've managed to earn about $10,000 from some side hustle, but that feels like a drop in the bucket compared to the $472,085 I lost. I feel like this is the dumbest move I've ever made, but I am still trying to keep my head high. So yeah, that's the tea: I ruined my family financially, learned a hard lesson about overconfidence, and now I am stuck in the aftermath, hoping one day to bounce back. But for now, it's just me, my regret, and a stack of empty bills.
